transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I keep steering clear of my own workshop, and I've been avoiding any family get-togethers if there's a chance my brother-in-law might be there. 

After all this time, I guess I'm just tired of planning my whole life around trying not to run into those reminders. It's just getting to be too much work to keep dodging them.
Could you tell me why you feel the need to avoid your workshop and your brother-in-law?

Well, I'm not really sure how to explain it. I just... I get this feeling like I shouldn't be around them. It's not something I can put my finger on exactly, I just know I need to stay away. I haven't really thought about the exact reason why, to be honest.
Did something specific happen in your workshop or involving your brother-in-law that makes you feel this way?
Well, yes. We had a... a confrontation out there. This whole thing has been going on since that happened with my brother-in-law, which was about two years and four months ago now.
Do you find yourself having unwanted, vivid memories or nightmares about that confrontation?

Yes, I do. Not really nightmares, but memories, yes. Out of nowhere, I'll just... I'll see his hand with that heavy tool again. It's like a picture that just pops into my head. I might just be going about my day, standing there shaving, or working on a painting, and suddenly it's right there in my mind. And honestly, it still makes my chest tighten up when it happens.

When those memories of the confrontation pop into your head, do you ever feel like you are actually reliving the event as if it is happening all over again in the present moment, or do you feel like you are somehow detached or observing it from outside of yourself?

No, it's not like that. I don't feel like I'm back there in the workshop, and I don't feel like I'm outside my body watching it either. It's just... a very clear memory that comes up. I know I'm standing at the sink or sitting at my easel, but the image is just stuck in my head.
Since that incident, have you found yourself feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, or more jumpy than you used to be?

No, I can't say that I have. I don't really feel jumpy or on edge all the time. I mean, my chest gets tight when those memories pop up, like I mentioned, but other than that... no. I don't startle easily or anything like that.
Since that incident, have you been feeling down, hopeless, or like you have lost interest in the things you used to enjoy?
No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm still painting, still keeping busy. I don't feel hopeless or down in the dumps, really. Just dealing with those memories when they happen.
Do you find yourself blaming yourself or anyone else for what happened during that confrontation in the workshop?

Well, mostly myself, I suppose. I just keep telling myself that I should have put my foot down a lot sooner and never let him stay with us in the first place. It's hard not to think that... well, maybe none of this would have happened if I had just handled it like a man from the start.

Have you noticed any persistent negative changes in your thoughts or beliefs about yourself or the world since that day, such as feeling like you can no longer trust anyone or that the world is inherently dangerous?

Yeah, I suppose I have. I always used to think family was the one place you could just... let your guard down. But now, well, I catch myself thinking that you really can't trust people anymore. Not even the ones who sit right there at your own table.
Has this persistent need to avoid your workshop and your brother-in-law caused you significant distress or difficulty in your daily life, such as in your job or your relationships?

Well, I still manage the basics around the house and all. But... it has caused some trouble. I've stopped doing my regular volunteer jobs because they involve the workshop, and I just don't go to big family events anymore. Even my painting... it comes in fits and starts now, mostly because I avoid the workshop where I kept most of my supplies. So, yeah, it's definitely made things difficult.
Do you find yourself feeling as though your future is limited, or that you might not have a normal life span or achieve your goals because of what happened?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm 76, so I know I don't have all the time in the world anyway, but... no, I don't feel like my life is being cut short because of what happened. I still plan on being around for a while, even if things are a bit different now.
During that confrontation in the workshop, did you fear for your life, or did you experience or witness a situation involving actual or threatened serious injury or sexual violence?

No, I wouldn't say I feared for my life. I mean... it was a really bad situation, and he was very aggressive, but no one was threatening to kill me or seriously injure me. There weren't any weapons involved or anything like that. It was just a very ugly, intense confrontation that really shook me up.
